messages.author: 5b4b413851d6a7a8
messages.subject: Extracting resiudals from linear model
parts:
Dear community,
I am studying sexual dimorphism in cranial shape and trying to visualize shape differences on size-free data. I extracted residuals from a linear model and added them to the mean shape. Afterward, I performed plotRefToTarget() and something seemed wrong, but I don't know what. I would be grateful if you could inspect my code and help me find the answer.

Code:
lm.com.alo <- procD.lm(shape ~ logcs, iter = 9999, seed = 1, RRPP = TRUE, data = gdf)
residuals <- arrayspecs(lm.com.alo$residuals, 88, 2)
identical(dimnames(residuals)[[3]], dimnames(gdf$shape)[[3]])  #TRUE

shape.sizefree <- residuals

for (i in dim(residuals)[3]) {
  shape.sizefree[,,i] <- residuals[,,i] + mshape(gdf$shape)
}
plotRefToTarget(mshape(shape.sizefree[,,gdf$sex == "M"]),
                mshape(shape.sizefree[,,gdf$sex == "F"]),
                method = "points",
                mag = 3,
                links = links,
                gridPars = grid.par.2)

plotAllSpecimens(A = shape.sizefree, label = FALSE, mean = TRUE,
                 plot_param = list(pt.bg = ifelse(klasifajer$sex == "M", "steelblue3", "brown2"), pt.cex = 0.8, mean.bg = "gold2", mean.cex = 1.5))

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Extracting resiudals from linear model
parts:
Dear Mihajlo,

I believe your for-loop is not what you expect it to be.  I think it only added the mean shape to the last specimen, because you did not specify a range in your for-loop parameters (you merely provided a single value).

Here is an example to demonstrate what I mean:

> library(geomorph)
> data(plethodon)
> GPA <- gpagen(plethodon$land)

Performing GPA
  |=========================================================================| 100%

Making projections... Finished!
> dim(GPA$coords)
[1] 12  2 40

## Like you did
> for(i in dim(GPA$coords)[3]) print(i)
[1] 40

## Like you should do
> for(i in (1:dim(GPA$coords)[3])) print(i)
[1] 1
[1] 2
[1] 3
[1] 4
[1] 5
[1] 6
[1] 7
[1] 8
[1] 9
[1] 10
[1] 11
[1] 12
[1] 13
[1] 14
[1] 15
[1] 16
[1] 17
[1] 18
[1] 19
[1] 20
[1] 21
[1] 22
[1] 23
[1] 24
[1] 25
[1] 26
[1] 27
[1] 28
[1] 29
[1] 30
[1] 31
[1] 32
[1] 33
[1] 34
[1] 35
[1] 36
[1] 37
[1] 38
[1] 39
[1] 40

Obviously I am not trying to add the mean in my demo, but by printing the iteration, you can see in your case there was one iteration, rather than a number matching the number of specimens.

Hope that helps,
Mike
